title: Nā hoʻomanaʻo
description: Ten short stories in which people remember: a strike on a sugar plantation, a letter to an old maths teacher, a first newspaper interview, a grandmother's grave, net fishing with a father on Molokaʻi, the upland birds of Kōkeʻe, a family story from the battle of Nuʻuanu, a father's shoe shop, a summer at the volcano with a geologist uncle and music at the zoo.

lessons.title: Nā lā ma ka mahiko
lessons.summary: Kaʻapana, now ninety, remembers leaving school at sixteen to cut and carry sugarcane at the Waialua plantation, the overseer weighing each man's cane, the workers' complaints and demands, the strike and the riot, and the small raise that followed.
lessons.text:
ʻO Kaʻapana koʻu inoa, a he 90 oʻu makahiki. Ua hānau ʻia au ma Waialua, ma Oʻahu. Hoʻomanaʻo maopopo nō au i koʻu mau lā ma ka mahiko o Waialua. He ʻumikūmāono oʻu makahiki i ka wā aʻu i hoʻōki ai i ke kula. ʻIlihune koʻu ʻohana, a ua pono ke kālā no ka ʻai, no laila ua hele au e hana ma ka mahiko.

I kēlā me kēia lā, ua ala mākou i ka hola 4 o ke kakahiaka. Ua ʻoki mākou i ke kō me nā pahi nui. A laila, ua ʻawe mākou i ke kō kaumaha ma ko mākou poʻohiwi a hiki i ke kaʻaahi. I ka pō, ua pehu koʻu mau poʻohiwi a me koʻu mau lima. Ua kau koʻu makuahine i ka ʻaila ma luna o koʻu mau poʻohiwi pehu, a ua moe au.

I ka pau ʻana o ka hana, ua kaupaona ka luna i ke kō a kēlā me kēia limahana. Ua uku ʻia mākou e like me ke kaumaha o ke kō. Inā liʻiliʻi ke kō i kaupaona ʻia, liʻiliʻi ka uku.

Ua hoʻohalahala nā limahana i ka uku liʻiliʻi a me nā hola lōʻihi. Ua hālāwai lākou i ka pō, a ua kākau lākou i kā lākou mau koina: he uku nui aʻe, he mau hola pōkole aʻe, a me nā hale maikaʻi aʻe no nā ʻohana. ʻAʻole i ʻae ka mea nona ka mahiko i nā koina. No laila, ua hoʻōki nā limahana a pau i kā lākou hana.

ʻEkolu mahina ka lōʻihi o ka hoʻōki ʻana i ka hana. I kekahi lā, ua hiki mai nā mākaʻi, a ua haunaele ma ke alanui ma mua o ka hale o ka luna. Ua hūnā koʻu makuahine iaʻu i loko o ka hale. ʻAʻole i poina iaʻu kēlā haunaele.

Ma hope o ka haunaele, ua ʻae ka mea nona ka mahiko i kekahi o nā koina: ua piʻi iki ka uku. ʻAʻole nui ka loli, akā ua haʻaheo nā limahana. I kēia manawa, ke noʻonoʻo au i koʻu mau poʻohiwi pehu, ʻakaʻaka au. Ikaika nō au ia wā.

Nā nīnau:
ʻEhia makahiki o Kaʻapana i ka wā āna i hoʻōki ai i ke kula?
He ʻumikūmāono ona makahiki.
Ua ʻawe nā limahana i ke kō ma hea?
Ua ʻawe lākou i ke kō ma ko lākou poʻohiwi a hiki i ke kaʻaahi.
Na wai i kaupaona i ke kō?
Na ka luna i kaupaona i ke kō a kēlā me kēia limahana.
No ke aha i hoʻohalahala ai nā limahana?
Ua hoʻohalahala lākou i ka uku liʻiliʻi a me nā hola lōʻihi.

lessons.title: He leka i ke kumu makemakika
lessons.summary: In a letter to her old maths teacher, Wailani, now a maths teacher herself, recalls how he drew a circle with its centre and diameter, had the class measure plates with string and ruler, average their ratios to 3.14, multiply diameters in inches, and always explained again with patience.
lessons.text:
Aloha e Kumu Kamakaʻala,

ʻO Wailani kēia. He haumāna au ma kou papa makemakika i ka makahiki 1998. ʻAʻole paha ʻoe e hoʻomanaʻo mai iaʻu, akā hoʻomanaʻo mau au iā ʻoe. I kēia makahiki, ua lilo au i kumu makemakika ma kekahi kula kaiapuni ma Kapolei, a makemake au e haʻi aku iā ʻoe i ke kumu.

Ma mua o kou papa, ua makaʻu au i ka makemakika. ʻAʻole i mōakaaka iaʻu nā helu. I ka lā mua, ua kaha ʻoe i kekahi poepoe nui ma ka papa ʻeleʻele, a ua kaha ʻoe i kekahi kiko ma ka waenakonu o ka poepoe. "ʻO kēia kiko ka waenakonu," wahi āu. A laila, ua kaha ʻoe i kekahi laina pololei mai kekahi ʻaoʻao o ka poepoe a hiki i kekahi ʻaoʻao, ma o ka waenakonu. "ʻO kēia laina ke anawaena. A ʻo ka laina a puni ka poepoe, ʻo ia ke anapuni."

Ua hāʻawi ʻoe i kēlā me kēia haumāna i kekahi pā poepoe a me kekahi kaula. Ua ana mākou i ke anapuni o ka pā me ke kaula, a i ke anawaena me ka lula. He 30 kenimika ke anapuni o kaʻu pā, a he 9.5 kenimika kona anawaena. A laila, ua helu mākou i ka lākiō o ke anapuni i ke anawaena. Ua kākau mākou i nā haʻina ma ka papa ʻeleʻele: 3.1, 3.2, 3.15, 3.12. Ua helu mākou i ka ʻawelika o nā haʻina a pau, a ʻo ka ʻawelika, 3.14! "Like ka lākiō no nā poepoe a pau," wahi āu. "Nui a liʻiliʻi paha ka poepoe, ʻaʻole loli ka lākiō."

I ka pule aʻe, ua hāʻawi ʻoe iā mākou i kekahi poepoe hou, i ana ʻia me nā ʻīniha. He 10 ʻīniha kona anawaena. Ua pāhoʻonui mākou i ka 10 me ka 3.14, a ua loaʻa ka haʻina: 31.4 ʻīniha. A laila, ua ana mākou i ke anapuni me ke kaula, a he 31.4 ʻīniha nō!

Ua ahonui loa ʻoe. I ka wā ʻaʻole i mōakaaka iaʻu kekahi mea, ua aʻo hou ʻoe iaʻu me ke ahonui. I kēia manawa, ke nīnau kaʻu mau haumāna i ka nīnau hoʻokahi i ʻekolu manawa, hoʻomanaʻo au iā ʻoe, a pane au me ke ahonui.

Me ke aloha nui,
Wailani

Nā nīnau:
He aha ka mea a ke kumu i kaha ai ma ka waenakonu o ka poepoe?
Ua kaha ʻo ia i kekahi kiko ma ka waenakonu.
He aha ka ʻawelika o nā haʻina o nā haumāna?
ʻO 3.14 ka ʻawelika.
Ua pāhoʻonui nā haumāna i ka 10 ʻīniha me ka aha?
Ua pāhoʻonui lākou i ka 10 me ka 3.14.
He aha ka hana a ke kumu i ka wā ʻaʻole i mōakaaka kekahi mea iā Wailani?
Ua aʻo hou ʻo ia me ke ahonui.

lessons.title: Kaʻu nīnauele mua
lessons.summary: Keomailani remembers her first newspaper interview in 1995, with Kahiwalani, a pioneer of a Hawaiian-only school for small children: she postponed it twice, knocked twice on the door, was clumsy and nervous, heard why every kahakō matters, and chose the headline for the column.
lessons.text:
I ka makahiki 1995, ua hoʻomaka au e hana ma kekahi nūpepa ʻōlelo Hawaiʻi ma Honolulu. ʻO Keomailani koʻu inoa, a he 23 oʻu makahiki ia wā. I kēlā me kēia pule, he kolamu ko ka nūpepa no nā paionia o ka ʻōlelo Hawaiʻi. Ua hāʻawi mai koʻu luna iaʻu i kekahi hana nui: he nīnauele me kekahi paionia no ia kolamu.

ʻO ka paionia, ʻo Kahiwalani, he kumu kahiko ma Lāʻie. I nā makahiki 1980, ua kōkua ʻo ia i ka hoʻokumu ʻana i kekahi kula no nā keiki liʻiliʻi, kahi i ʻōlelo ʻia ai ka ʻōlelo Hawaiʻi wale nō.

Ua pīhoihoi loa au. Ua hoʻopaneʻe au i ka nīnauele i ʻelua manawa, no ka mea, ua manaʻo au ʻaʻole au i mākaukau. I ke kolu o ka manawa, ʻaʻole au i hoʻopaneʻe hou. Ua hele au i kona hale, a ua kīkē au ma ka puka. ʻAʻohe pane. Ua kīkē hou au, me ka ikaika. A laila, ua wehe ʻo ia i ka puka.

Ua hemahema loa au. Ua hāʻule kaʻu puke liʻiliʻi, a ua poina iaʻu kekahi o kaʻu mau nīnau. Akā, ua ʻakaʻaka ʻo Kahiwalani. "Mai pīhoihoi, e kuʻu kaikamahine," wahi āna. "Hemahema nō kākou a pau i ka hoʻomaka ʻana." A laila, ua haʻi mai ʻo ia i kona moʻolelo. I kēlā mau makahiki, ʻaʻole i kākau ka poʻe he nui i ke kahakō. Ua aʻo ʻo Kahiwalani i nā keiki e kākau i kēlā me kēia kahakō. "Inā ʻaʻohe kahakō, loli paha ka manaʻo o ka huaʻōlelo," wahi āna.

Ma ka hale, ua kākau au i ka moʻolelo no ke kolamu. Ua hoʻokaʻina au i kāna mau ʻōlelo, mai ka hoʻomaka a hiki i ka hopena. Ua noʻonoʻo lōʻihi au i kaʻu poʻomanaʻo, a ua koho au i kēia poʻomanaʻo: "Mai poina i ke kahakō." Ua hoʻokaʻina hou koʻu luna i kekahi mau paukū, akā ua mālama ʻo ia i kaʻu poʻomanaʻo. Aia nō ia kolamu i loko o kekahi pahu ma koʻu hale a hiki i kēia lā.

Nā nīnau:
He aha ka hana mua a Keomailani ma ka nūpepa?
Ua nīnauele ʻo ia i kekahi paionia no ke kolamu.
No ke aha ʻo ia i hoʻopaneʻe ai i ka nīnauele?
No ka mea, ua pīhoihoi ʻo ia, a ua manaʻo ʻo ia ʻaʻole ʻo ia i mākaukau.
He aha kāna hana ma ka puka o ka hale?
Ua kīkē ʻo ia ma ka puka i ʻelua manawa.
He aha ka ʻōlelo a Kahiwalani i ka wā i hemahema ai ʻo Keomailani?
"Mai pīhoihoi. Hemahema nō kākou a pau i ka hoʻomaka ʻana."
He aha ka poʻomanaʻo o ke kolamu?
ʻO "Mai poina i ke kahakō" kona poʻomanaʻo.

lessons.title: Ka ilina o Tūtū
lessons.summary: On her grandmother's birthday Keakalani visits her grave in Makawao and remembers the fan she was cooled with on hot nights, the blessing before sleep, the stroke that left Tūtū's right side numb, the lonely house after her death, and lays fragrant flowers and a new fan on the stone.
lessons.text:
I ka lā 3 o ʻApelila, ka lā hānau o koʻu tūtū wahine ʻo Lokalia, hele au i kona ilina ma Makawao. Aia ka ilina ma kahi kokoke i ka hale pule kahiko, ma lalo o kekahi kumu lāʻau nui. I kēlā me kēia makahiki, lawe au i nā pua keʻokeʻo onaona i ka ilina, no ka mea, ua aloha ʻo Tūtū i nā pua onaona.

ʻO Keakalani koʻu inoa, a ua noho au me Tūtū Lokalia i koʻu wā kamaliʻi. Pumehana kona hale, a pumehana kona aloha. I nā ahiahi wela, noho ʻo ia ma waho o ka hale me kāna peʻahi, a peʻahi ʻo ia iā ia iho. I ka pō, ke wela loa a ʻaʻole hiki iaʻu ke moe, peʻahi mālie ʻo ia iaʻu me kāna peʻahi a moe au. Ma mua o koʻu moe ʻana, kau ʻo ia i kona lima ma koʻu poʻo, a hoʻopōmaikaʻi ʻo ia iaʻu: "E hoʻopōmaikaʻi ke Akua iā ʻoe, e kuʻu moʻopuna."

I nā makahiki hope o kona ola, ua loaʻa iā ia kekahi maʻi, a ua lōlō kona lima ʻākau a me kona wāwae ʻākau. ʻAʻole hiki iā ia ke paʻa i ka peʻahi. No laila, ua peʻahi au iā ia, e like me kāna hana iaʻu ma mua. Ua lōlō kona lima, akā ʻaʻole i nalowale kona ʻakaʻaka.

Ua make ʻo ia i koʻu makahiki 25. Mehameha loa ka hale ma hope o kona make ʻana. Ua mina au i kona leo, a ua mina au i nā pō pumehana me ia. I kekahi manawa, ke mehameha au, lawe au i kāna peʻahi kahiko, a peʻahi au iaʻu iho.

I kēia makahiki, ua hele hou au i ka ilina. Ua hoʻomoe au i nā pua onaona ma luna o ka pōhaku, a ua hoʻomoe pū au i kekahi peʻahi hou aʻu i ulana ai. Ua pule au: "E ke Akua, e hoʻopōmaikaʻi mai iā Tūtū." Ma hope, ua noho au ma laila a hiki i ke ahiahi. ʻAʻole au i mehameha ia lā.

Nā nīnau:
Aia ka ilina o Tūtū Lokalia i hea?
Aia ia ma Makawao, ma kahi kokoke i ka hale pule kahiko.
He aha ka hana a Tūtū me kāna peʻahi i ka pō?
Ua peʻahi ʻo ia i kāna moʻopuna a moe.
He aha ka mea i lōlō ma hope o ka maʻi?
Ua lōlō kona lima ʻākau a me kona wāwae ʻākau.
He aha nā mea i mina ʻia e Keakalani?
Ua mina ʻo ia i ka leo o Tūtū a me nā pō pumehana me ia.
He aha nā mea i hoʻomoe ʻia ma luna o ka pōhaku?
Nā pua onaona a me kekahi peʻahi hou.

lessons.title: Ka ʻupena a koʻu makuakāne
lessons.summary: Kekoʻolani remembers Saturdays on Molokaʻi with his father: anchoring the canoe in a sheltered bay at Kamalō, swimming over the coral, pulling the heavy throw net until he panted, the shining fish scales, the old basket woven by his grandfather, and scaling the fish at home as the sun went down.
lessons.text:
ʻO Kekoʻolani koʻu inoa. I koʻu wā kamaliʻi ma Molokaʻi, ua hele au me koʻu makuakāne e lawaiʻa i kēlā me kēia Pōʻaono. He waʻa liʻiliʻi kona, a ua hoʻokele ʻo ia i ka waʻa i kekahi kai mālie ma Kamalō. Ua pale ʻia ia wahi mai ka makani, a ua hoʻolulu māua i ka waʻa ma laila. "Ke hoʻolulu kāua ma ʻaneʻi, ʻaʻole e neʻe ka waʻa," wahi a koʻu makuakāne.

Ma lalo o ke kai, he nui nā koʻa, a he nui nā iʻa ma waena o nā koʻa. Ua ʻauʻau au ma luna o nā koʻa, a ua nānā au i nā iʻa. "Mai kū ma luna o ke koʻa," wahi a koʻu makuakāne. "He ola ko ke koʻa."

A laila, ua hoʻolei koʻu makuakāne i kāna ʻupena. Ua wehe ʻia ka ʻupena ma ka lewa, a ua hāʻule ia i loko o ke kai. Ma hope o kekahi manawa, ua ʻume māua i ka ʻupena. Kaumaha ka ʻupena! Ua ʻume a ʻume māua a hiki i ka waʻa. Ua nae au ma hope o ka ʻume ʻana. "Ke nae ʻoe, e hoʻomaha iki," wahi āna.

I loko o ka ʻupena, he nui nā iʻa. Ua ʻōlinolino nā unahi o nā iʻa i ka lā, e like me ke kālā. Ua waiho māua i nā iʻa i loko o ka hīnaʻi. He hīnaʻi kahiko ia, i ulana ʻia e koʻu kupuna kāne.

I ka ʻaui ʻana o ka lā, ua hoʻi māua i ka hale. Ma waho o ka hale, ua kahi māua i nā unahi o nā iʻa. Ua lele nā unahi ʻōlinolino ma nā wahi a pau, ma ko māua mau lima a me ko māua lauoho. Ua ʻakaʻaka koʻu makuahine, a ua kuke ʻo ia i nā iʻa no ka ʻaina ahiahi.

Ua make koʻu makuakāne, akā aia nō kāna ʻupena a me ka hīnaʻi kahiko ma koʻu hale. I kēia manawa, ke ʻaui ka lā ma ka Pōʻaono, hoʻomanaʻo au i ko māua mau lā ma ke kai.

Nā nīnau:
Ma hea lāua i hoʻolulu ai i ka waʻa?
Ua hoʻolulu lāua ma kekahi kai mālie ma Kamalō.
He aha ka ʻōlelo a ka makuakāne no ke koʻa?
"Mai kū ma luna o ke koʻa. He ola ko ke koʻa."
No ke aha i nae ai ʻo Kekoʻolani?
Ua nae ʻo ia ma hope o ka ʻume ʻana i ka ʻupena kaumaha.
Ua waiho lāua i nā iʻa i loko o ka aha?
Ua waiho lāua i nā iʻa i loko o ka hīnaʻi kahiko.
He aha kā lāua hana ma waho o ka hale?
Ua kahi lāua i nā unahi o nā iʻa.

lessons.title: Ka ʻiʻiwi a me ka ʻōʻō
lessons.summary: Kaʻohelani remembers a walk with her grandfather through the upland forest of Kōkeʻe: a scarlet ʻiʻiwi with its curved beak, his memory of the now extinct ʻōʻō, the lookout over Kalalau with an old stone cairn, a flag fluttering in the wind, and dark clouds sending them home.
lessons.text:
ʻO Kaʻohelani koʻu inoa. I koʻu makahiki 10, ua lawe koʻu tūtū kāne iaʻu i Kōkeʻe ma Kauaʻi. Ua aloha nui ʻo Tūtū i ka wao, ka nahele ma uka o nā kuahiwi. "ʻO ka wao ka hale o nā manu," wahi āna. Ua hele wāwae māua ma kekahi ala liʻiliʻi i loko o ka wao.

Ma luna o kekahi kumu lāʻau, ua ʻike māua i kekahi manu ʻulaʻula. "He ʻiʻiwi kēlā," wahi a Tūtū. ʻUlaʻula nā hulu o ka ʻiʻiwi, a ʻeleʻele kona mau ʻēheu. Lōʻihi kona nuku, a naha ka nuku e like me ka mahina hou. "Naha ka nuku o ka ʻiʻiwi e like me ke ʻano o nā pua o ka wao," wahi a Tūtū.

A laila, ua haʻi mai ʻo Tūtū no ka ʻōʻō. "He manu ʻeleʻele ka ʻōʻō, me nā hulu melemele ma lalo o kona mau ʻēheu. Ua lohe au i ka leo o ka ʻōʻō i koʻu wā ʻōpio, ma kēia wao nō." I kēia manawa, ʻaʻohe ʻōʻō e ola nei ma Kauaʻi, a ʻaʻohe ʻōʻō e ola nei ma nā wahi a pau o ka honua. Ua kaumaha ka leo o Tūtū.

Ma hope o hoʻokahi hola, ua hiki māua i ke kilohana. Mai ke kilohana, ua ʻike māua i ke awāwa nui o Kalalau a me ke kai polū ma lalo loa. Ma ka ʻaoʻao o ke kilohana, aia kekahi ahu pōhaku kahiko. Ua makemake au e kau i kekahi pōhaku ma luna o ka ahu. "Mai hana pēlā," wahi a Tūtū. "Na nā kūpuna i kūkulu i kēia ahu. E nānā wale nō kāua."

Ma ke kilohana, e welo ana kekahi hae Hawaiʻi i ka makani. Ua welo ka hae, a ua welo pū ka lauoho keʻokeʻo o Tūtū. A laila, ua ʻele ka lani, a ua hiki mai nā ao ʻele mai ke kai mai. "E hoʻi kāua ma mua o ka ua," wahi a Tūtū. Ua hoʻi māua ma ke ala ma waena o ka wao, a ua lohe hou māua i ka leo o ka ʻiʻiwi.

Nā nīnau:
Ua lawe ʻia ʻo Kaʻohelani i hea e kona tūtū kāne?
Ua lawe ʻia ʻo ia i Kōkeʻe ma Kauaʻi.
He aha ke ʻano o ka nuku o ka ʻiʻiwi?
Lōʻihi ka nuku, a naha e like me ka mahina hou.
He aha ka manu i lohe ʻia e Tūtū i kona wā ʻōpio?
Ua lohe ʻo ia i ka leo o ka ʻōʻō.
He aha ka mea ma ka ʻaoʻao o ke kilohana?
Aia ma laila kekahi ahu pōhaku kahiko.
He aha ka mea i welo i ka makani?
Ua welo ka hae Hawaiʻi a me ka lauoho keʻokeʻo o Tūtū.

lessons.title: Ka moʻolelo ma ka Pali
lessons.summary: At the Nuʻuanu Pali lookout, Kaleʻa's father tells how Kamehameha conquered Oʻahu in 1795 and how their ancestor Kapuaʻala, a warrior of Kalanikūpule, survived, burned for revenge and then gave it up; the family still keeps his old sword, and Kaleʻa wonders whether the story is true.
lessons.text:
I koʻu makahiki 12, ua lawe koʻu makuakāne iaʻu i ka Pali o Nuʻuanu. Ua kū māua ma ke kilohana, a ua pā ikaika ka makani. Keu a ka ikaika o ka makani ma ia wahi! "Ma ʻaneʻi i naʻi ai ʻo Kamehameha iā Oʻahu," wahi āna. "Laulaha kēia moʻolelo."

A laila, ua haʻi mai ʻo ia i ka moʻolelo. I ka makahiki 1795, ua hele mai ʻo Kamehameha me nā kānaka he nui i Oʻahu, no ka mea, ua makemake ʻo ia e naʻi i nā mokupuni a pau. Ua hoʻouluulu ke aliʻi o Oʻahu, ʻo Kalanikūpule, i kona poʻe koa ma ke awāwa ʻo Nuʻuanu. Ua ālai lākou i ke ala me nā pōhaku a me nā lāʻau. Akā, ua loaʻa i nā koa o Kamehameha nā mea kaua a me nā pahikaua o nā haole. ʻAʻole hiki i nā koa o Oʻahu ke ālai iā lākou. Ua hoʻomake ʻia nā koa he nui. Keu a ka nui o ka poʻe i make.

"He moʻolelo kēia no ko kāua ʻohana kekahi," wahi a koʻu makuakāne. "He koa ko kāua kupuna, ʻo Kapuaʻala, no Kalanikūpule. ʻAʻole ʻo ia i make. Ua hūnā ʻo ia iā ia iho ma ke kuahiwi no nā lā he nui." Ma hope o ke kaua, ua piha kona naʻau i ka inaina. Ua inaina ʻo ia iā Kamehameha, a ua makemake ʻo ia e pānaʻi.

Akā, ua noho ʻo Kapuaʻala me kekahi ʻohana ma Kailua, a ua male ʻo ia. I ka hānau ʻia ʻana o kāna keiki mua, ua hala kona inaina. Ua ʻōlelo ʻo ia i kāna mau keiki: "Mai hoʻomake i ke kanaka no ka pānaʻi." Laulaha kēia ʻōlelo ma ko mākou ʻohana. Ua mālama pū ka ʻohana i kekahi pahikaua kahiko a Kapuaʻala i lawe ai mai ke kaua mai. Aia ia pahikaua ma ka hale o koʻu kupuna wahine a hiki i kēia lā.

Ua kānalua au. "He moʻolelo ʻoiaʻiʻo kēia?" i nīnau ai au. Ua ʻakaʻaka koʻu makuakāne. "Kānalua nō wau i kekahi manawa," wahi āna. "Akā, ʻoiaʻiʻo ka manaʻo o ka moʻolelo." ʻO Kaleʻa koʻu inoa, a i kēia manawa, haʻi aku au i kēia moʻolelo i kaʻu mau keiki.

Nā nīnau:
Ua naʻi ʻo Kamehameha iā Oʻahu i ka makahiki hea?
Ua naʻi ʻo ia iā Oʻahu i ka makahiki 1795.
Na wai i hoʻouluulu i nā koa o Oʻahu?
Na Kalanikūpule i hoʻouluulu i nā koa o Oʻahu.
He aha ka ʻōlelo a Kapuaʻala i kāna mau keiki?
"Mai hoʻomake i ke kanaka no ka pānaʻi."
Aia ka pahikaua kahiko i hea?
Aia ia ma ka hale o ke kupuna wahine o Kaleʻa.

lessons.title: Ka hale kūʻai kāmaʻa
lessons.summary: Kamakahi remembers his father's shoe shop in Wailuku: brushing shoes after school, soles that came off or wore thin, the big stores in Kahului, the loan whose principal could not be repaid, the bankruptcy papers his father signed, and the last day when he gave away the shoes after forty-four happy years.
lessons.text:
ʻO Kamakahi koʻu inoa. No kanahākūmāhā makahiki, ua mālama koʻu makuakāne i kekahi hale kūʻai kāmaʻa ma ke alanui nui o Wailuku. I koʻu wā kamaliʻi, ua hele au i ka hale kūʻai ma hope o ke kula i kēlā me kēia lā.

ʻO kaʻu hana, ʻo ka palaki ʻana i nā kāmaʻa. He mau palaki kā koʻu makuakāne no kēlā me kēia ʻano kāmaʻa: he palaki paʻakikī no nā kāmaʻa hana, a he palaki palupalu no nā kāmaʻa ʻili. Ua palaki au a ʻōlinolino nā kāmaʻa.

Ua lawe mai nā kānaka i ko lākou mau kāmaʻa kahiko. I kekahi manawa, ua hemo ka ʻili o lalo o ke kāmaʻa. I kekahi manawa, ua lahilahi loa ka ʻili o lalo, no ka nui o ka hele wāwae ʻana. Ua hoʻopili koʻu makuakāne i nā ʻili hemo, a ua kau ʻo ia i nā ʻili hou ma lalo o nā kāmaʻa lahilahi. Ua hoʻohauʻoli kāna hana i nā kānaka.

Akā, i nā makahiki 1990, ua wehe ʻia kekahi mau hale kūʻai nui ma Kahului, a ua emi ke kumu kūʻai o nā kāmaʻa ma laila. Ua emi ka poʻe i hele mai i ko mākou hale kūʻai. Ua hōʻaiʻē koʻu makuakāne i ke kālā mai ka panakō mai, akā ʻaʻole hiki iā ia ke hoʻihoʻi i ke kumupaʻa. Ua uku ʻo ia i kekahi kālā i kēlā me kēia mahina, akā ʻaʻole i emi ke kumupaʻa. I ka makahiki 1999, ua panakalupa ʻo ia.

I ka lā hope loa, ua kau koʻu makuakāne i kona pūlima ma nā pepa o ka panakalupa. A laila, ua hele mai nā kānaka he nui o Wailuku. Ua hāʻawi wale koʻu makuakāne i nā kāmaʻa hope loa i nā keiki o ke kaiāulu, a ua hoʻohauʻoli kēlā i nā keiki.

Ua ʻōlelo ʻo ia iaʻu: "Ua panakalupa au, akā ua hoʻohauʻoli kēia hana iaʻu no kanahākūmāhā makahiki." Aia nō kāna palaki kahiko ma koʻu hale. Ke palaki au i koʻu mau kāmaʻa, hoʻomanaʻo au iā ia.

Nā nīnau:
ʻEhia makahiki i mālama ai ka makuakāne i ka hale kūʻai?
Ua mālama ʻo ia i ka hale kūʻai no kanahākūmāhā makahiki.
He aha ka hana a Kamakahi ma hope o ke kula?
Ua palaki ʻo ia i nā kāmaʻa.
No ke aha i panakalupa ai ka makuakāne?
No ka mea, ʻaʻole hiki iā ia ke hoʻihoʻi i ke kumupaʻa i ka panakō.
He aha kāna hana ma ka lā hope loa?
Ua kau ʻo ia i kona pūlima ma nā pepa, a ua hāʻawi wale ʻo ia i nā kāmaʻa i nā keiki.

lessons.title: Ka pele a me ka pālolo
lessons.summary: Kawaikapu remembers the summer she turned eighteen, when her uncle Leihulu, a geologist with a doctorate, took her to Kīlauea: the lava welling up, his patient answers about the sea floor and the moving continents, red clay from old lava, an evening rest watching the glow, and her own path into geology.
lessons.text:
ʻO Kawaikapu koʻu inoa. I koʻu makahiki ʻumikūmāwalu, ua pau koʻu kula kiʻekiʻe, akā ʻaʻole au i ʻike i ka mea aʻu e aʻo ai ma ke kulanui. I kēlā kauwela, ua kono mai ʻo Leihulu, ke kaikunāne o koʻu makuahine, iaʻu e hele pū me ia i ka mokupuni ʻo Hawaiʻi. Ua loaʻa iā Leihulu kekahi kēkelē laeʻula ma ke kālaihonua, a ua hana ʻo ia ma Kīlauea.

Ia kauwela, ua hū ka pele mai kekahi lua ma ka ʻaoʻao o ka mauna. Ua kū māua ma kahi mamao, a ua nānā māua i ka pele ʻulaʻula e hū ana a e kahe ana ma luna o ka ʻāina. "Ke hū ka pele, ulu ka mokupuni," wahi a Leihulu.

Ua nīnau au i nā nīnau he nui loa. "No ke aha he mau mokupuni ma ʻaneʻi, ma waena o ka moana, ma kahi mamao loa mai nā mokuhonua?" Ua ahonui ʻo Leihulu, a ua pane ʻo ia i kēlā me kēia nīnau. "Ma lalo o ke kai, aia ka papakū o ke kai," wahi āna. "Ma lalo o ka papakū, aia kekahi wahi wela loa, a hū ka pele mai laila mai. Neʻe mālie ka papakū, a hana ʻia nā mokupuni hou. ʻAʻole kū mau nā mokuhonua. Neʻe mālie lākou, ʻoi aku ka mālie ma mua o ka ulu ʻana o kou lauoho."

I kekahi lā, ua hele māua i kekahi ʻāina kahiko, kahi i ʻulaʻula ai ka lepo. "He pālolo kēia," wahi a Leihulu. "Ua lilo ka pele kahiko i pālolo ma hope o nā makahiki he nui loa." Ua lawe ʻo ia i kekahi pālolo i loko o kekahi ʻeke no kāna hana. Ua hana au i kekahi ipu liʻiliʻi me ka pālolo.

Ma hope o ka hana o ka lā, ua noho māua ma kahi kiʻekiʻe e maha. Ua maha māua a pō, a ua nānā māua i ka ʻulaʻula o ka pele ma ka pō ʻeleʻele. "No ke aha ʻoe i aʻo ai i ke kālaihonua?" i nīnau ai au. "No ka mea, he moʻolelo ko kēlā me kēia pōhaku," wahi āna.

I ka makahiki aʻe, ua hoʻomaka au e aʻo i ke kālaihonua ma ke kulanui. I kēia manawa, ua loaʻa iaʻu kekahi kēkelē laeʻula, e like me Leihulu.

Nā nīnau:
ʻEhia makahiki o Kawaikapu i kēlā kauwela?
He ʻumikūmāwalu ona makahiki.
He aha ke kēkelē o Leihulu?
He kēkelē laeʻula ma ke kālaihonua.
He aha ka pālolo, wahi a Leihulu?
Ua lilo ka pele kahiko i pālolo ma hope o nā makahiki he nui loa.
He aha kā lāua hana ma hope o ka hana o ka lā?
Ua noho lāua ma kahi kiʻekiʻe e maha a hiki i ka pō.

lessons.title: Ka puolo ma ka hale holoholona
lessons.summary: Analani remembers summer Wednesdays when her father took her and her little sister to the zoo in Waikīkī: the antelopes from far Africa, goats and sheep with a wet nose and soft wool, the music clubs playing on the lawn in the evening, the singer's sweet voice, and falling asleep on her father's lap.
lessons.text:
ʻO Analani koʻu inoa. I nā kauwela o koʻu wā kamaliʻi, ua lawe koʻu makuakāne iā māua ʻo koʻu kaikaina i ka hale holoholona ma Waikīkī i kēlā me kēia Pōʻakolu. I ke ahiahi o ka Pōʻakolu, hoʻokani ʻia ka puolo ma ka pā nui o ka hale holoholona, a hele mai nā ʻohana he nui e hoʻolohe i ka puolo.

Ma mua o ka puolo, ua hele mākou e nānā i nā holoholona. Ua makemake nui koʻu kaikaina i nā ʻanekelopa. Ua hele mai nā ʻanekelopa mai ʻApelika mai, he mokuhonua mamao loa. Lōʻihi nā wāwae o nā ʻanekelopa, a holo wikiwiki lākou. "Holo ka ʻanekelopa e like me ka makani," wahi a koʻu makuakāne.

Ma kekahi pā liʻiliʻi, aia nā kao a me nā hipa. Hiki i nā keiki ke komo i ka pā a hānai i nā kao a me nā hipa. Palupalu ka hulu o nā hipa, e like me ke ao. Ua hoʻopili kekahi kao i kona ihu i koʻu lima, a pulu ka ihu o ke kao. Ua ʻai ke kao i ka lau mai koʻu lima. Ua hele mai kekahi hipa, a ua ʻai ʻo ia i ka lole o koʻu kaikaina! Ua ʻakaʻaka nui māua.

I ka pau ʻana o ka lā, ua noho mākou ma ka pā nui no ka puolo. I kēlā me kēia pule, he kalapu ʻokoʻa: i kekahi pule, he kalapu pila o nā kāne kahiko; i kekahi pule ʻē aʻe, he kalapu hula o nā ʻōpio. Ua makemake nui au i kekahi kalapu o nā wāhine mai Kaimukī. Hone ka leo o kā lākou mea mele, a hone ke kani o kā lākou mau pila. ʻO ka puolo hone kaʻu puolo punahele.

Ma mua o ka pau ʻana o ka puolo, ua moe mau koʻu kaikaina ma ka ʻūhā o koʻu makuakāne. I kekahi manawa, ua moe pū au ma kona ʻūhā. I kēia manawa, lawe au i kaʻu mau keiki i ka puolo ma ka hale holoholona. Moe kaʻu keiki liʻiliʻi ma koʻu ʻūhā, a hoʻomanaʻo au i koʻu makuakāne.

Nā nīnau:
Ua hele lākou i ka hale holoholona i ka lā hea?
Ua hele lākou i kēlā me kēia Pōʻakolu.
Mai hea mai nā ʻanekelopa?
Mai ʻApelika mai, he mokuhonua mamao loa.
He aha ka mea a ke kao i hoʻopili ai i ka lima o Analani?
Ua hoʻopili ke kao i kona ihu i kona lima.
Pehea ka leo o ka mea mele o ke kalapu o nā wāhine?
Hone kona leo.
Ma hea i moe ai ke kaikaina?
Ua moe ʻo ia ma ka ʻūhā o ko lāua makuakāne.
